title: Monitoring and Observability in Spring Boot

cards.title: Introduction to Spring Boot Actuator
cards.content:
Spring Boot Actuator brings production-ready features to your application without requiring you to write custom monitoring tools.

It provides built-in HTTP endpoints and JMX beans to monitor and interact with your running application.

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
</dependency>

Key features include health checks, metric collection, environment properties inspection, and thread dumps.

cards.title: Essential Actuator Endpoints
cards.content:
Actuator provides several built-in endpoints to inspect application state:

  • /actuator/health: Shows application health information.
  • /actuator/info: Displays arbitrary application info.
  • /actuator/metrics: Shows metric information (JVM memory, CPU, HTTP requests).
  • /actuator/env: Exposes properties from Spring's Environment.
  • /actuator/httpexchanges: Displays HTTP request/response exchange details.

cards.title: Creating Custom Health Indicators
cards.content:
You can create custom health checks by implementing the HealthIndicator interface.

@Component
public class DatabaseHealthIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    @Override
    public Health health() {
        boolean dbIsUp = checkDbConnection();
        if (dbIsUp) {
            return Health.up().withDetail("Database", "Reachable").build();
        }
        return Health.down().withDetail("Database", "Unreachable").build();
    }
}

cards.title: Metrics Collection with Micrometer & Prometheus
cards.content:
Micrometer acts as a facade over popular monitoring systems (like SLF4J for logging). It allows you to instrument code once and export metrics to backends like Prometheus, Datadog, or InfluxDB.

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
    <artifactId>micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
</dependency>

Adding this dependency automatically configures a /actuator/prometheus endpoint formatted for Prometheus scraping.

cards.title: Distributed Tracing with Micrometer Tracing
cards.content:
In microservice architectures, request tracing across service boundaries is critical.

Micrometer Tracing (successor to Spring Cloud Sleuth in Spring Boot 3) automatically propagates context across HTTP headers and adds trace IDs and span IDs to logs.

  • Trace ID: Uniquely identifies an entire request journey across services.
  • Span ID: Uniquely identifies a single unit of work within a service.

Traces can be exported to systems like Zipkin or Jaeger for visualization.
